ax1b.bar(monthly['Date'], monthly['Orders'], width=20, color=PALETTE['secondary'], alpha=0.30, label='Orders')
ax1.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v,_: f'R\${v:.0f}K'))
ax1.set_title('Monthly Revenue & Order Volume Trend')
ax1b.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor=PALETTE['secondary'])
l1,la1 = ax1.get_legend_handles_labels(); l2,la2 = ax1b.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax1.legend(l1+l2, la1+la2, fontsize=9, loc='upper left')
ax1.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3, ls='--', color=PALETTE['grid'])
plt.setp(ax1.get_xticklabels(), rotation=25, ha='right', fontsize=8)

wedge_colors = [PALETTE['primary'],PALETTE['secondary'],PALETTE['success'],PALETTE['warning']]
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax2.pie(
    pay_dist.values, labels=pay_labels, colors=wedge_colors[:len(pay_dist)],
    autopct='%1.1f%%', pctdistance=0.78, startangle=140,
    wedgeprops=dict(width=0.55, edgecolor='white', linewidth=2))
for t in autotexts: t.set_fontsize(9); t.set_fontweight('bold')
ax2.set_title('Payment Type\nDistribution')

bars = ax3.barh(top_cats.index[::-1], top_cats.values[::-1]/1e3,
                color=CAT_COLORS[:len(top_cats)], height=0.65, edgecolor='white')
ax3.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v,_: f'R\${v:.0f}K'))
ax3.set_title('Top 8 Product Categories by Revenue')
ax3.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3, ls='--', color=PALETTE['grid'])
for bar in bars:
    w = bar.get_width()
    ax3.annotate(f'R\${w:.0f}K', xy=(w, bar.get_y()+bar.get_height()/2),
                 xytext=(4,0), textcoords='offset points', va='center', fontsize=8.5, fontweight='bold')

score_colors = [PALETTE['danger'],'#F97316',PALETTE['warning'],'#84CC16',PALETTE['success']]
b4 = ax4.bar(delivery_review['review_score'], delivery_review['delivery_days'],
             color=score_colors, width=0.7, edgecolor='white')
ax4.set_xlabel('Review Score'); ax4.set_ylabel('Avg Delivery Days')
ax4.set_title('Delivery Speed vs\nCustomer Review')
ax4.set_xticks([1,2,3,4,5]); ax4.set_xticklabels(['1 star','2 star','3 star','4 star','5 star'], fontsize=8)
ax4.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3, ls='--', color=PALETTE['grid'])
for bar in b4:
    h = bar.get_height()
    ax4.annotate(f'{h:.1f}d', xy=(bar.get_x()+bar.get_width()/2, h),
                 xytext=(0,3), textcoords='offset points', ha='center', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold')

x5 = np.arange(len(state_rev))
b5 = ax5.bar(x5, state_rev.values/1e3,
             color=[PALETTE['primary'] if s=='SP' else PALETTE['secondary'] if s=='RJ'
                    else PALETTE['success'] for s in state_rev.index],
             width=0.65, edgecolor='white')
ax5.set_xticks(x5); ax5.set_xticklabels(state_rev.index, fontsize=10)
ax5.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v,_: f'R\${v:.0f}K'))
ax5.set_title('Revenue by Customer State (Top 8)')
ax5.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3, ls='--', color=PALETTE['grid'])
for bar in b5:
    h = bar.get_height()
    ax5.annotate(f'R\${h:.0f}K', xy=(bar.get_x()+bar.get_width()/2, h),
                 xytext=(0,4), textcoords='offset points', ha='center', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold')

plt.savefig('olist_dashboard.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150, facecolor=PALETTE['bg'])
print('Dashboard saved!')

# Heatmap
fig_h, ax_h = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 5))
fig_h.patch.set_facecolor('#F9FAFB')
top6 = df['category_label'].value_counts().head(6).index
df_top = df[df['category_label'].isin(top6)]
hm = df_top.pivot_table(values='total_value', index='category_label', columns='Month_Name', aggfunc='sum')
month_order = ['Jan','Feb','Mar','Apr','May','Jun','Jul','Aug','Sep','Oct','Nov','Dec']
hm = hm.reindex(columns=[m for m in month_order if m in hm.columns])
sns.heatmap(hm/1e3, annot=True, fmt='.0f', cmap='Blues', linewidths=0.6, linecolor='white', ax=ax_h, cbar_kws={'label':'Revenue (R\$K)'})
ax_h.set_title('Monthly Revenue Heatmap by Top 6 Categories (R\$K)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('olist_heatmap.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
print('Heatmap saved!')

Oke, sekarang aku sudah paham banget profil parfum kamu! Berdasarkan koleksi yang kamu punya — black musk, black vanilla, black sakura, oud, dan Dance Floor yang sweet coconut-vanilla — preferensi kamu sangat jelas: **soft, warm, sweet/gourmand, tidak menusuk**. Ini rekomendasi yang spesifik untuk kamu:

---

**Berdasarkan koleksimu, kamu pasti bakal cocok dengan:**

**🥇 Mykonos Moroccan Vanilla** — Ini paling "aman" buat kamu. Floral vanilla yang sweet tapi tidak giung, soft, cocok daily. Banyak yang rate 9/10 dan bilang ini varian vanilla terbaik Mykonos. Mirip vibes Dance Floor kamu tapi dengan sentuhan oud ringan, cocok banget sama yang udah biasa pakai black musk + black vanilla.

**🥈 Mykonos Dreamscape** — Gabungan mango, lemon, jasmine, praline, lalu dry down ke amber, cedar, tonka, dan vanilla yang warm dan creamy. Banyak reviewer bilang ini makin enak setelah beberapa menit — softens beautifully. Banyak yang dapat compliment dan tidak mau berhenti nyium tangan sendiri.

**🥉 Mykonos Luminos** — Aroma manis creamy dari blue java banana accord yang unik, dengan dry down vanilla dan oud yang soft. Mirip karakter Dance Floor kamu (sweet-creamy) tapi lebih complex dan berkarakter.

---

**Yang perlu kamu SKIP:**

- **Slow Living** — Dominan citrus, ada yang bilang seperti "es lemon" — terlalu fresh untuk kamu.
- **Satin Blanc** — Ini tricky. Wanginya powdery, milky, dan clean — vibesnya "habis mandi di hotel bintang lima", tapi ada reviewer yang bilang bisa bikin mual di siang hari karena SPL-nya kencang banget, dan buat kamu yang suka soft — projection-nya justru terlalu kuat.
- **California Signature, Inception** — Terlalu segar/aromatic, bukan selera kamu.

---

**Satu saran penting untuk pemula Mykonos:**

Longevity Mykonos bagus, tapi SPL (sillage/projection) beberapa variannya cukup kencang. Untuk yang suka soft, **semprot 1–2 kali saja** di kulit, bukan di baju. Dan karena kamu belum pernah nyoba, **beli travel size 15ml dulu** sebelum commit ke botol full. Banyak dijual di Shopee/Tokopedia sekitar 30–50rb.

**Urutan cobain yang disarankan buat kamu: Moroccan Vanilla → Dreamscape → Luminos.**

The person asked for help diagnosing a tablet display issue where the screen appeared very dim or seemingly off, but content was still visible when a flashlight was shone on it. chat_messages.text:
Itu klasik banget — **backlight (lampu latar) LCD-nya mati**, bukan layarnya.

LCD itu butuh dua komponen: panel LCD-nya sendiri (yang bikin gambar) + backlight di belakangnya (yang bikin terang). Kalau backlight mati, gambar tetap ada tapi gelap banget — makanya keliatan kalau disenter.

**Penyebab paling umum:**

**1. Inverter rusak** (tablet/laptop lama)
Komponen yang ngubah daya ke backlight. Kalau ini mati, backlight ikut mati.

**2. LED backlight putus/rusak**
LCD modern pakai strip LED di pinggir/belakang. Bisa putus satu titik atau semuanya.

**3. Kabel backlight longgar/putus**
Kabel tipis yang nyambungin backlight ke board — sering lepas kalau pernah jatuh.

**4. IC driver backlight di motherboard rusak**
Chipnya yang ngatur arus ke LED — kalau ini, perlu servis board.

**5. Software brightness bug** *(jarang)*
Kadang terjebak di brightness 0 — coba pencet tombol brightness fisik beberapa kali.

---

**Cara diagnosa cepat:**

- Coba colok charger → kalau menyala normal = masalah daya/baterai
- Lihat apakah ada garis/retak di layar → kalau ada, LCD-nya yang rusak fisik
- Coba restart/hard reset → kalau software bug, ini bisa fix

---

**Solusinya?**
Paling umum harus ke tukang servis untuk ganti backlight/inverter. Biayanya biasanya jauh lebih murah dari ganti LCD full. Tab apa yang kamu punya?

summary:
**Conversation Overview**

This conversation involved a student named Abdan Rifai (NPM: 2301170017, Prodi: Teknologi Informasi, Matkul: Internet of Things) working through a multi-part IoT practical assignment covering Pertemuan 10 and 11 material on cloud storage and dashboard monitoring. The conversation progressed through building a complete end-to-end IoT system integrating Wokwi (ESP32 simulator), a public MQTT broker, a local Node.js dashboard, and ThingsBoard Cloud.

Claude first generated an interactive HTML summary widget of the P10/P11 lecture materials, then built a full IoT dashboard project (Node.js + Express + Socket.io + Chart.js) with simulated sensor data. The project was then upgraded to v2 with real MQTT integration using broker.emqx.io, Wokwi ESP32 sketch (DHT22 + LDR + LED actuators), and ThingsBoard Cloud telemetry. The chosen platform was ThingsBoard with sensors for suhu (temperature), kelembaban (humidity), and cahaya (light intensity). Key troubleshooting included fixing port 3000 EADDRINUSE errors (using `taskkill /IM node.exe /F`), resolving a `cannot get /` static file serving issue by changing to `app.use(express.static('public'))`, correcting ThingsBoard curl JSON format from three separate objects to one combined object, and clarifying that ESP32 uses English key names (`temperature`, `humidity`, `light`) for ThingsBoard while the local dashboard uses Indonesian names (`suhu`, `kelembaban`, `cahaya`). Finally, Claude generated a formatted 3-page PDF lab report including identity block, theory, architecture, implementation details, screenshots, verification checklist, conclusions, and references.

Materi IoT

Pertemuan 10 & 11

Cloud Storage · Dashboard Monitoring

Mengapa perlu Cloud?
Data IoT sangat masif — sensor terus mengirim data setiap detik. Menyimpan secara lokal tidak praktis dan mahal.
Manfaat Utama
Data Ingestion & Storage — menerima & simpan volume data masif secara scalable
Device Management — provisioning, monitoring status, update firmware OTA
Analytics & Visualisasi — data → wawasan via rule engine & dashboard real-time
Security — hanya perangkat terautentikasi yang bisa konek, semua terenkripsi
3 Platform yang Dipelajari
🔷
ThingsBoard
Open-source & Fleksibel
MQTT CoAP HTTP Open-source Self-hosted
Dashboard drag-and-drop kaya fitur
Rule Engine untuk notifikasi & otomasi
DB: PostgreSQL, Cassandra, TimescaleDB
🔶
Firebase
Google · Real-time · Mobile-first
HTTPS REST NoSQL/JSON
Realtime Database — sinkronisasi instan
Security Rules granular
Cloud Functions — auto trigger
⚡
AWS IoT Core
Enterprise · Amazon
MQTT+TLS HTTPS WebSocket
Device Shadow — "virtual twin" offline
Autentikasi sertifikat X.509
Integrasi S3, Lambda, DynamoDB
Tidak ada yang "paling baik" — pilihan tergantung volume data, keamanan, anggaran, dan keahlian tim.
Fitur TB ThingsBoard FB Firebase AWS
Model Open-source / cloud Backend Google Cloud enterprise
Database PostgreSQL, Cassandra, Timescale NoSQL / JSON S3, DynamoDB, Timestream
Visualisasi Drag-drop kaya fitur Perlu HTML/JS sendiri QuickSight / layanan lain
Kesulitan Sedang Mudah Sulit / curam
Target Developer, startup, industri Mobile dev, prototipe cepat Enterprise, skala global
Keunggulan Fleksibel, gratis, self-install Sinkronisasi real-time cepat Skalabilitas & keamanan kelas dunia
Panduan Memilih
Prototipe cepat, real-time update → Firebase
Kontrol penuh, dashboard built-in, hemat → ThingsBoard
Skala global, keamanan tinggi, enterprise → AWS IoT
Pertemuan 11: Membangun dashboard web interaktif menggunakan Node.js + Socket.io + Chart.js dengan update data setiap 2 detik.
Komponen Dashboard
Indikator Status — lampu hijau/merah online/offline
Gauge Meter — nilai persentase (kapasitas tangki, suhu)
Metric Card — nilai terbaru, rata-rata, atau perubahan
Tombol Kontrol — switch/slider kirim perintah ke perangkat
Line Chart — perubahan suhu terhadap waktu
Bar Chart — perbandingan nilai antar sensor
Scatter Plot — korelasi dua variabel
Histogram — distribusi data
Frontend: HTML, CSS, JS + Chart.js / ECharts / ApexCharts
Real-time: WebSocket via Socket.io atau MQTT over WebSocket
Backend: Node.js (Express) atau Python (FastAPI/Flask)
Database: InfluxDB (time-series) atau PostgreSQL + Timescale
Rekomendasi kuliah: Node.js + Socket.io + Chart.js — paling mudah dipahami mahasiswa.
🔌 Sensor IoT
↓
📡 Gateway / Broker MQTT
↓
⚙️ Backend API / WebSocket
↓
🗄 Database (opsional)
↓
📊 Dashboard Web
Data bisa dikirim via HTTP Polling, SSE, atau WebSocket (paling umum).
Studi Kasus: Smart Greenhouse — suhu (line chart), kelembaban tanah (gauge), intensitas cahaya (bar), tombol lampu via MQTT. Update tiap 2 detik.
Langkah Membangun Dashboard
1
Install Node.js & npm
Download versi LTS dari nodejs.org. Verifikasi dengan node -v dan npm -v
2
Struktur Proyek
Folder: iot-dashboard/ berisi server.js, folder public/ (index.html, style.css, script.js)
3
Backend — server.js
Express + Socket.io. Simulasi data sensor suhu & kelembaban via setInterval setiap 2000ms, lalu emit event sensor-update
4
Frontend — HTML + JS
index.html: load Socket.io & Chart.js CDN. script.js: dengarkan event sensor-update, update widget & chart (max 20 poin)
5
Jalankan
# Install & run npm init -y npm install express socket.io node server.js # Buka: localhost:3000
Fitur Lanjutan
Gauge Meter MQTT Broker Nyata InfluxDB History Threshold Alert Notif Telegram Responsive CSS
Threshold: suhu > 35°C → widget merah + bunyi peringatan
Framework lanjutan: Grafana, Node-RED, ThingsBoard

# 🌿 IoT Dashboard — Smart Greenhouse

Dashboard monitoring IoT real-time menggunakan Node.js + Socket.io + Chart.js.
Dibuat sesuai materi Pertemuan 10 & 11.

---

## 📁 Struktur Proyek

```
iot-dashboard/
├── server.js          ← Backend: Express + Socket.io + simulasi sensor
├── package.json
└── public/
    ├── index.html     ← Struktur halaman HTML
    ├── style.css      ← Tampilan dark theme
    └── script.js      ← Chart.js + Socket.io client
```

---

## 🚀 Cara Menjalankan

### 1. Pastikan Node.js sudah terinstall
```bash
node -v
npm -v
```

### 2. Install dependencies
```bash
npm install
```

### 3. Jalankan server
```bash
node server.js
```

### 4. Buka browser
```
http://localhost:3000
```

---

## ✨ Fitur

| Fitur | Keterangan |
|-------|------------|
| 📈 Line Chart | Suhu real-time, update tiap 2 detik, simpan 20 titik terakhir |
| 📊 Bar Chart | Perbandingan nilai 3 sensor terkini |
| ⏲ Gauge | Kelembaban tanah dalam bentuk setengah lingkaran |
| 💡 Kontrol Lampu | Toggle ON/OFF via Socket.io ke server |
| 🚿 Kontrol Pompa | Toggle ON/OFF via Socket.io ke server |
| ⚠ Threshold Alert | Suhu > 35°C → kartu merah + log peringatan |
| 📋 Event Log | Riwayat 8 event terakhir |
| 📱 Responsive | Grid menyesuaikan layar mobile & desktop |

---

## 🔧 Kustomisasi

### Ubah interval update (server.js baris ~37)
```js
}, 2000);  // ganti 2000 ke nilai lain (ms)
```

### Ubah threshold suhu (script.js)
```js
checkAlert('alertSuhu', data.suhu > 35, ...);  // ganti 35
```

### Hubungkan ke sensor nyata (server.js)
Ganti blok `simulateSensor()` dengan pembacaan data dari MQTT broker:
```js
const mqtt = require('mqtt');
const client = mqtt.connect('mqtt://broker.emqx.io');
client.subscribe('greenhouse/sensor');
client.on('message', (topic, msg) => {
  const data = JSON.parse(msg.toString());
  io.emit('sensor-update', data);
});
```

---

## 📚 Referensi
- Chart.js: https://www.chartjs.org/
- Socket.io: https://socket.io/get-started/chat
- MQTT over WebSocket: https://www.emqx.com/en/blog/connect-to-mqtt-broker-with-websocket


## 🚀 LANGKAH 1 — Jalankan Dashboard Lokal

```bash
npm install          # install express, socket.io, mqtt
node server.js       # jalankan server
```
Buka **http://localhost:3000** — dashboard aktif mode simulasi dulu.

---

## 🔷 LANGKAH 2 — Setup ThingsBoard Cloud

1. Buka **https://thingsboard.cloud/** → daftar akun gratis
2. **Devices** → `+` → Create Device → beri nama `esp32-greenhouse`
3. Klik device → tab **Credentials** → copy **Access Token**
4. Paste token ke `wokwi/sketch.ino` baris:
   ```cpp
   const char* TB_TOKEN = "PASTE_TOKEN_DISINI";
   ```
5. Buat Dashboard ThingsBoard:
   - **Dashboards** → `+` → Create Dashboard → nama `Smart Greenhouse`
   - Tambah widget:
     - **Timeseries Line Chart** → key: `temperature`, `humidity`
     - **Timeseries Bar Chart** → key: `light`
     - **Value Card** → key: `temperature`
     - **Switch** → untuk kontrol (opsional, perlu RPC setup)

---

## 🟢 LANGKAH 3 — Setup Wokwi Simulator

1. Buka **https://wokwi.com** → New Project → ESP32
2. Tab **diagram.json** → paste isi file `wokwi/diagram.json`
3. Tab **sketch.ino** → paste isi file `wokwi/sketch.ino`

   - `DHTesp`
   - `PubSubClient`
   - `ArduinoJson`


|-----|------|
| ESP32 → Broker | Serial Monitor Wokwi: `[PUB] greenhouse/sensor` |

| ESP32 → ThingsBoard | ThingsBoard → Device → Latest Telemetry |
| Dashboard → ESP32 | Klik tombol Lampu → LED kuning di Wokwi menyala |

---

## 🔧 Konfigurasi Topic MQTT

| Topic | Arah | Isi |
|-------|------|-----|
| `greenhouse/sensor` | ESP32 → Server | `{"suhu":27.3,"kelembaban":65.1,"cahaya":480,...}` |
| `greenhouse/lampu/cmd` | Server → ESP32 | `ON` atau `OFF` |
| `greenhouse/pompa/cmd` | Server → ESP32 | `ON` atau `OFF` |
| `v1/devices/me/telemetry` | ESP32 → ThingsBoard | `{"temperature":27.3,"humidity":65.1,...}` |

---

| Sensor | Kondisi | Aksi |
|--------|---------|------|
| Suhu | > 35°C | Kartu merah + log peringatan |
| Kelembaban | < 40% | Kartu merah + log peringatan |
| Cahaya | > 1000 lux | Kartu merah + log peringatan |

     2	name: pdf
     3	description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
     4	license: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms
     5	---
     6	
     7	# PDF Processing Guide
     8	
     9	## Overview
    10	
    11	This guide covers essential PDF processing operations using Python libraries and command-line tools. For advanced features, JavaScript libraries, and detailed examples, see REFERENCE.md. If you need to fill out a PDF form, read FORMS.md and follow its instructions.
    12	
    13	## Quick Start
    14	
    15	```python
    16	from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter
    17	
    18	# Read a PDF
    19	reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
    20	print(f"Pages: {len(reader.pages)}")
    21	
    22	# Extract text
    23	text = ""
    24	for page in reader.pages:
    25	    text += page.extract_text()
    26	```
    27	
    28	## Python Libraries
    29	
    30	### pypdf - Basic Operations
    31	
    32	#### Merge PDFs
    33	```python
    34	from pypdf import PdfWriter, PdfReader
    35	
    36	writer = PdfWriter()
    37	for pdf_file in ["doc1.pdf", "doc2.pdf", "doc3.pdf"]:
    38	    reader = PdfReader(pdf_file)
    39	    for page in reader.pages:
    40	        writer.add_page(page)
    41	
    42	with open("merged.pdf", "wb") as output:
    43	    writer.write(output)
    44	```
    45	
    46	#### Split PDF
    47	```python
    48	reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
    49	for i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):
    50	    writer = PdfWriter()
    51	    writer.add_page(page)
    52	    with open(f"page_{i+1}.pdf", "wb") as output:
    53	        writer.write(output)
    54	```
    55	
    56	#### Extract Metadata
    57	```python
    58	reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
    59	meta = reader.metadata
    60	print(f"Title: {meta.title}")
    61	print(f"Author: {meta.author}")
    62	print(f"Subject: {meta.subject}")
    63	print(f"Creator: {meta.creator}")
    64	```
    65	
    66	#### Rotate Pages
    67	```python
    68	reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
    69	writer = PdfWriter()
    70	
    71	page = reader.pages[0]
    72	page.rotate(90)  # Rotate 90 degrees clockwise
    73	writer.add_page(page)
    74	
    75	with open("rotated.pdf", "wb") as output:
    76	    writer.write(output)
    77	```
    78	
    79	### pdfplumber - Text and Table Extraction
    80	
    81	#### Extract Text with Layout
    82	```python
    83	import pdfplumber
    84	
    85	with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    86	    for page in pdf.pages:
    87	        text = page.extract_text()
    88	        print(text)
    89	```
    90	
    91	#### Extract Tables
    92	```python
    93	with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    94	    for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):
    95	        tables = page.extract_tables()
    96	        for j, table in enumerate(tables):
    97	            print(f"Table {j+1} on page {i+1}:")
    98	            for row in table:
    99	                print(row)
   100	```
   101	
   102	#### Advanced Table Extraction
   103	```python
   104	import pandas as pd
   105	
   106	with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
   107	    all_tables = []
   108	    for page in pdf.pages:
   109	        tables = page.extract_tables()
   110	        for table in tables:
   111	            if table:  # Check if table is not empty
   112	                df = pd.DataFrame(table[1:], columns=table[0])
   113	                all_tables.append(df)
   114	
   115	# Combine all tables
   116	if all_tables:
   117	    combined_df = pd.concat(all_tables, ignore_index=True)
   118	    combined_df.to_excel("extracted_tables.xlsx", index=False)
   119	```
   120	
   121	### reportlab - Create PDFs
   122	
   123	#### Basic PDF Creation
   124	```python
   125	from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
   126	from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas
   127	
   128	c = canvas.Canvas("hello.pdf", pagesize=letter)
   129	width, height = letter
   130	
   131	# Add text
   132	c.drawString(100, height - 100, "Hello World!")
   133	c.drawString(100, height - 120, "This is a PDF created with reportlab")
   134	
   135	# Add a line
   136	c.line(100, height - 140, 400, height - 140)
   137	
   138	# Save
   139	c.save()
   140	```
   141	
   142	#### Create PDF with Multiple Pages
   143	```python
   144	from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
   145	from reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak
   146	from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet
   147	
   148	doc = SimpleDocTemplate("report.pdf", pagesize=letter)
   149	styles = getSampleStyleSheet()
   150	story = []
   151	
   152	# Add content
   153	title = Paragraph("Report Title", styles['Title'])
   154	story.append(title)
   155	story.append(Spacer(1, 12))
   156	
   157	body = Paragraph("This is the body of the report. " * 20, styles['Normal'])
   158	story.append(body)
   159	story.append(PageBreak())
   160	
   161	# Page 2
   162	story.append(Paragraph("Page 2", styles['Heading1']))
   163	story.append(Paragraph("Content for page 2", styles['Normal']))
   164	
   165	# Build PDF
   166	doc.build(story)
   167	```
   168	
   169	#### Subscripts and Superscripts
   170	
   171	**IMPORTANT**: Never use Unicode subscript/superscript characters (₀₁₂₃₄₅₆₇₈₉, ⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹) in ReportLab PDFs. The built-in fonts do not include these glyphs, causing them to render as solid black boxes.
   172	
   173	Instead, use ReportLab's XML markup tags in Paragraph objects:
   174	```python
   175	from reportlab.platypus import Paragraph
   176	from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet
   177	
   178	styles = getSampleStyleSheet()
   179	
   180	# Subscripts: use <sub> tag
   181	chemical = Paragraph("H<sub>2</sub>O", styles['Normal'])
   182	
   183	# Superscripts: use <super> tag
   184	squared = Paragraph("x<super>2</super> + y<super>2</super>", styles['Normal'])
   185	```
   186	
   187	For canvas-drawn text (not Paragraph objects), manually adjust font the size and position rather than using Unicode subscripts/superscripts.
   188	
   189	## Command-Line Tools
   190	
   191	### pdftotext (poppler-utils)
   192	```bash
   193	# Extract text
   194	pdftotext input.pdf output.txt
   195	
   196	# Extract text preserving layout
   197	pdftotext -layout input.pdf output.txt
   198	
   199	# Extract specific pages
   200	pdftotext -f 1 -l 5 input.pdf output.txt  # Pages 1-5
   201	```
   202	
   203	### qpdf
   204	```bash
   205	# Merge PDFs
   206	qpdf --empty --pages file1.pdf file2.pdf -- merged.pdf
   207	
   208	# Split pages
   209	qpdf input.pdf --pages . 1-5 -- pages1-5.pdf
   210	qpdf input.pdf --pages . 6-10 -- pages6-10.pdf
   211	
   212	# Rotate pages
   213	qpdf input.pdf output.pdf --rotate=+90:1  # Rotate page 1 by 90 degrees
   214	
   215	# Remove password
   216	qpdf --password=mypassword --decrypt encrypted.pdf decrypted.pdf
   217	```
   218	
   219	### pdftk (if available)
   220	```bash
   221	# Merge
   222	pdftk file1.pdf file2.pdf cat output merged.pdf
   223	
   224	# Split
   225	pdftk input.pdf burst
   226	
   227	# Rotate
   228	pdftk input.pdf rotate 1east output rotated.pdf
   229	```
   230	
   231	## Common Tasks
   232	
   233	### Extract Text from Scanned PDFs
   234	```python
   235	# Requires: pip install pytesseract pdf2image
   236	import pytesseract
   237	from pdf2image import convert_from_path
   238	
   239	# Convert PDF to images
   240	images = convert_from_path('scanned.pdf')
   241	
   242	# OCR each page
   243	text = ""
   244	for i, image in enumerate(images):
   245	    text += f"Page {i+1}:\n"
   246	    text += pytesseract.image_to_string(image)
   247	    text += "\n\n"
   248	
   249	print(text)
   250	```
   251	
   252	### Add Watermark
   253	```python
   254	from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter
   255	
   256	# Create watermark (or load existing)
   257	watermark = PdfReader("watermark.pdf").pages[0]
   258	
   259	# Apply to all pages
   260	reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
   261	writer = PdfWriter()
   262	
   263	for page in reader.pages:
   264	    page.merge_page(watermark)
   265	    writer.add_page(page)
   266	
   267	with open("watermarked.pdf", "wb") as output:
   268	    writer.write(output)
   269	```
   270	
   271	### Extract Images
   272	```bash

This conversation documents an extensive, ongoing Flutter development session in which the person is building "Jejak Nusantara," a Learning Management System (LMS) focused on Indonesian history for students at the elementary through high school level. The person is a first-time app developer working toward publishing on Google Play Store. The project uses Flutter 3.x targeting Android and web platforms, with Firebase as the backend (Auth, Firestore, Cloud Functions) and a plan to integrate AI chatbot functionality using Gemini API (free tier for development) with eventual migration to Claude Sonnet 4.6 for production.

The session covered the full project lifecycle from planning through active development. Early in the conversation, the person defined the app's scope: a multi-role system with three user types (Siswa/student, Guru/teacher, Admin), each with separate dashboards and routing. Key design decisions included an earthy color palette (dark brown #3D2B1F, wood #5C3D2E, antique gold #C4956A, cream #F5E6C8), a mascot named "Mpu" (a Bugis explorer figure), and a quiz anti-cheat system that detects when students leave the app or switch browser tabs, then shuffles questions and answers using Fisher-Yates algorithm and resets the timer. The person requested and received a 12-slide PowerPoint presentation, a detailed blueprint wireframe covering 26 screens, and a master brief document summarizing all project decisions.

The development work proceeded through Phase 1 (project setup, Firebase integration, multi-role authentication with login and register screens) and into Phase 2 (student dashboard, chapter list, chapter detail, quiz system, teacher dashboard with realtime student monitoring, and chatbot UI). Technical issues encountered and resolved included: deprecated `.withOpacity()` replaced with `.withValues(alpha:)`, type mismatches between `String` and `UserModel` return types in auth service, Firestore permission-denied errors caused by expired Security Rules (rules had a July 9, 2026 expiration date), Firestore composite index requirements for combined `where` + `orderBy` queries, quiz questions not loading due to field name typos (`urutan ` with trailing space vs `urutan`), and CORS errors when calling Gemini API directly from Flutter Web. The person's Firebase project is named `jejak-nusantara-id`, the Flutter project is located at `C:\jejak_nusantara`, the GitHub repo is at `https://github.com/ItsMePanda-hub/jejak-nusantara`, and the app's package name is `com.jejaknusantara.jejak_nusantara`. Firebase region is `asia-southeast1`. The conversation ended mid-session with the person attempting to add admin routing and encountering a `GoException: no routes for location` error, indicating Go Router is configured but missing the admin route definition.

The person works on Windows 11, uses VS Code as the primary editor with Android Studio for emulator management, and runs commands primarily through PowerShell. Firebase Storage was skipped in favor of a workaround using YouTube links and Google Drive links stored as Firestore string fields, to avoid requiring a Blaze billing plan upgrade during development. Admin accounts are created manually via Firebase Console (not through the app's register flow) with `role: "admin"` and `status: "active"` set directly in Firestore, with the admin email `admin@jejaknusantara.com` established for testing.

# Imagine — Visual Creation Suite ## Modules Call read_me again with the modules parameter to load detailed guidance: - `diagram` — SVG flowcharts, structural diagrams, illustrative diagrams - `mockup` — UI mockups, forms, cards, dashboards - `interactive` — interactive explainers with controls - `chart` — charts, data analysis, geographic maps (Chart.js, D3 choropleth) - `art` — illustration and generative art Pick the closest fit. The module includes all relevant design guidance. **Complexity budget — hard limits:** - Box subtitles: ≤5 words. Detail goes in click-through (`sendPrompt`) or the prose below — not the box. - Colors: ≤2 ramps per diagram. If colors encode meaning (states, tiers), add a 1-line legend. Otherwise use one neutral ramp. - Horizontal tier: ≤4 boxes at full width (~140px each). 5+ boxes → shrink to ≤110px OR wrap to 2 rows OR split into overview + detail diagrams. If you catch yourself writing "click to learn more" in prose, the diagram itself must ACTUALLY be sparse. Don't promise brevity then front-load everything. **Accessibility:** For HTML widgets, begin with a visually-hidden `

` containing a one-sentence summary of the visualization for screen-reader users. (SVG widgets use `role="img"` with `` and `<desc>` instead — see SVG setup.) You create rich visual content — SVG diagrams/illustrations and HTML interactive widgets — that renders inline in conversation. The best output feels like a natural extension of the chat. ## Core Design System These rules apply to ALL use cases. ### Philosophy - **Seamless**: Users shouldn't notice where claude.ai ends and your widget begins. - **Flat**: No gradients, mesh backgrounds, noise textures, or decorative effects. Clean flat surfaces. - **Compact**: Show the essential inline. Explain the rest in text. - **Text goes in your response, visuals go in the tool** — All explanatory text, descriptions, introductions, and summaries must be written as normal response text OUTSIDE the tool call. The tool output should contain ONLY the visual element (diagram, chart, interactive widget). Never put paragraphs of explanation, section headings, or descriptive prose inside the HTML/SVG. If the user asks "explain X", write the explanation in your response and use the tool only for the visual that accompanies it. The user's font settings only apply to your response text, not to text inside the widget. ### Streaming Output streams token-by-token. Structure code so useful content appears early. - **HTML**: `<style>` (short) → content HTML → `<script>` last. - **SVG**: `<defs>` (markers) → visual elements immediately. - Prefer inline `style="..."` over `<style>` blocks — inputs/controls must look correct mid-stream. - Keep `<style>` under ~15 lines. Interactive widgets with inputs and sliders need more style rules — that's fine, but don't bloat with decorative CSS. - Gradients, shadows, and blur flash during streaming DOM diffs. Use solid flat fills instead. ### Rules - No `<!-- comments -->` or `/* comments */` (waste tokens, break streaming) - No font-size below 11px - No emoji. Icons = Tabler **outline** webfont (5800+, already loaded): `<i class="ti ti-home"></i>`. Outline only — never use `-filled` suffixes (`ti-heart-filled` etc. are not loaded and will render blank). Inherits color + font-size from parent. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden="true"`; icon-only buttons get `aria-label`. Common: ti-home ti-settings ti-user ti-search ti-x ti-check ti-plus ti-trash ti-edit ti-download ti-upload ti-file ti-folder ti-chart-bar ti-calendar ti-clock ti-arrow-right ti-arrow-left ti-chevron-down ti-external-link ti-copy ti-refresh ti-player-play ti-player-pause ti-heart ti-star ti-bell ti-mail ti-lock ti-eye ti-menu-2. Don't hand-draw icon SVG paths. - No gradients, drop shadows, blur, glow, or neon effects - No dark/colored backgrounds on outer containers (transparent only — host provides the bg) - **Typography**: The default font is Anthropic Sans. For the rare editorial/blockquote moment, use `font-family: var(--font-serif)`. - **Headings**: h1 = 22px, h2 = 18px, h3 = 16px — all `font-weight: 500`. Heading color is pre-set to `var(--color-text-primary)` — don't override it. Body text = 16px, weight 400, `line-height: 1.7`. **Two weights only: 400 regular, 500 bold.** Never use 600 or 700 — they look heavy against the host UI. - **Sentence case** always. Never Title Case, never ALL CAPS. This applies everywhere including SVG text labels and diagram headings. - **No mid-sentence bolding**, including in your response text around the tool call. Entity names, class names, function names go in `code style` not **bold**. Bold is for headings and labels only. - The widget container is `display: block; width: 100%`. Your HTML fills it naturally — no wrapper div needed. Just start with your content directly. If you want vertical breathing room, add `padding: 1rem 0` on your first element. - Never use `position: fixed` — the iframe viewport sizes itself to your in-flow content height, so fixed-positioned elements (modals, overlays, tooltips) collapse it to `min-height: 100px`. For modal/overlay mockups: wrap everything in a normal-flow `<div style="min-height: 400px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.45); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;">` and put the modal inside — it's a faux viewport that actually contributes layout height. - No DOCTYPE, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` — just content fragments. - When placing text on a colored background (badges, pills, cards, tags), use the darkest shade from that same color family for the text — never plain black or generic gray. - **Corners**: use `border-radius: var(--border-radius-md)` (or `-lg` for cards) in HTML. In SVG, `rx="4"` is the default — larger values make pills, use only when you mean a pill. - **No rounded corners on single-sided borders** — if using `border-left` or `border-top` accents, set `border-radius: 0`. Rounded corners only work with full borders on all sides. - **No titles or prose inside the tool output** — see Philosophy above. - **Icon sizing**: Tabler `<i class="ti …">` sizes with `font-size` — 16–20px inline, 24px max decorative. For one-off inline SVG icons, set `width`/`height` explicitly (same limits). - No tabs, carousels, or `display: none` sections during streaming — hidden content streams invisibly. Show all content stacked vertically. (Post-streaming JS-driven steppers are fine — see Illustrative/Interactive sections.) - No nested scrolling — auto-fit height. - Scripts execute after streaming — load libraries via `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` (UMD globals), then use the global in a plain `<script>` that follows. - **CDN allowlist (CSP-enforced)**: external resources may ONLY load from `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `esm.sh`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com`. All other origins are blocked by the sandbox — the request silently fails. ### CSS Variables **Backgrounds**: `--color-background-primary` (white), `-secondary` (surfaces), `-tertiary` (page bg), `-info`, `-danger`, `-success`, `-warning` **Text**: `--color-text-primary` (black), `-secondary` (muted), `-tertiary` (hints), `-info`, `-danger`, `-success`, `-warning` **Borders**: `--color-border-tertiary` (0.15α, default), `-secondary` (0.3α, hover), `-primary` (0.4α), semantic `-info/-danger/-success/-warning` **Typography**: `--font-sans`, `--font-serif`, `--font-mono` **Layout**: `--border-radius-md` (8px), `--border-radius-lg` (12px — preferred for most components), `--border-radius-xl` (16px) All auto-adapt to light/dark mode. Flutter · Firebase · Web + Android

Setup & Auth

Phase 2 · Minggu 3–6

Konten & Pembelajaran

Upload materi PDF/video, manajemen kelas & mata pelajaran, tugas, pengumpulan, kuis online, dan papan nilai dasar.

FirestoreFirebase StoragePDF viewerVideo playerQuiz engine
Phase 3 · Minggu 7–10

Interaksi & AI Chatbot

Forum diskusi per kelas, notifikasi push, dan chatbot AI dengan maskot (Claude API) untuk bantu siswa belajar.

FCMClaude APIMaskot animasiForum
Phase 4 · Minggu 11–16

Polish & Deploy

Web build (Flutter Web), optimasi performa, testing, Play Store submission, dan setup domain untuk versi web.

Frontend

Flutter 3.x✓ Pilihan utama
1 codebase → Android + Web

State management, lebih clean dari Provider

Deep link support, web URL routing

Backend (BaaS)

Firebase AuthGratis
Login email, Google Sign-In
Firestore
Database realtime, sync otomatis
Firebase Storage
Upload PDF, gambar, video
Cloud Functions
Logic backend (auto-grading, notif)

AI Chatbot

Claude API (Haiku)Murah
Claude Haiku = cepat & hemat token

Deploy

Firebase Hosting
Flutter Web — gratis SSL + CDN
Google Play Store
APK release dengan keystore

7 Fitur Utama

Multi-role Auth

Admin, Guru, Siswa. Setiap role punya dashboard & akses berbeda.

Materi Pembelajaran

Upload PDF, embed YouTube, baca materi inline di app.

Tugas & Pengumpulan

Buat tugas, upload jawaban (PDF/foto), batas waktu otomatis.

Kuis Online

Pilihan ganda, timer, auto-grading, langsung tampil nilai.

Nilai & Rapor

Rekap nilai per siswa, export PDF, grafik perkembangan.

Forum Diskusi

Thread per mata pelajaran, guru bisa moderasi jawaban.

AI Chatbot Maskot

Karakter animasi dengan Claude API, jawab pertanyaan pelajaran, bisa dikustomisasi per sekolah.

Checklist Deploy ke Play Store

1

Buat keystore

Generate signing key dengan keytool. Simpan file .jks — JANGAN hilang, tidak bisa diganti!

2

Setup key.properties

Tambahkan keystore path + password ke file key.properties di folder android/.

3

Build App Bundle

flutter build appbundle --release. Hasilnya file .aab di build/app/outputs/bundle/.

4

Daftar Google Play Console

Biaya $25 sekali bayar. Buat aplikasi baru, isi semua metadata, screenshot, dan deskripsi.

5

Upload & Review

Upload .aab ke track Internal Testing dulu, lalu Production. Review Google biasanya 1–7 hari.

6

Deploy Flutter Web

flutter build web → firebase deploy. Dapat domain gratis *.web.app atau pakai domain sendiri.

# Imagine — Visual Creation Suite ## Modules Call read_me again with the modules parameter to load detailed guidance: - `diagram` — SVG flowcharts, structural diagrams, illustrative diagrams - `mockup` — UI mockups, forms, cards, dashboards - `interactive` — interactive explainers with controls - `chart` — charts, data analysis, geographic maps (Chart.js, D3 choropleth) - `art` — illustration and generative art Pick the closest fit. The module includes all relevant design guidance. **Complexity budget — hard limits:** - Box subtitles: ≤5 words. Detail goes in click-through (`sendPrompt`) or the prose below — not the box. - Colors: ≤2 ramps per diagram. If colors encode meaning (states, tiers), add a 1-line legend. Otherwise use one neutral ramp. - Horizontal tier: ≤4 boxes at full width (~140px each). 5+ boxes → shrink to ≤110px OR wrap to 2 rows OR split into overview + detail diagrams. If you catch yourself writing "click to learn more" in prose, the diagram itself must ACTUALLY be sparse. Don't promise brevity then front-load everything. **Accessibility:** For HTML widgets, begin with a visually-hidden `

` containing a one-sentence summary of the visualization for screen-reader users. (SVG widgets use `role="img"` with `` and `<desc>` instead — see SVG setup.) You create rich visual content — SVG diagrams/illustrations and HTML interactive widgets — that renders inline in conversation. The best output feels like a natural extension of the chat. ## Core Design System These rules apply to ALL use cases. ### Philosophy - **Seamless**: Users shouldn't notice where claude.ai ends and your widget begins. - **Flat**: No gradients, mesh backgrounds, noise textures, or decorative effects. Clean flat surfaces. - **Compact**: Show the essential inline. Explain the rest in text. - **Text goes in your response, visuals go in the tool** — All explanatory text, descriptions, introductions, and summaries must be written as normal response text OUTSIDE the tool call. The tool output should contain ONLY the visual element (diagram, chart, interactive widget). Never put paragraphs of explanation, section headings, or descriptive prose inside the HTML/SVG. If the user asks "explain X", write the explanation in your response and use the tool only for the visual that accompanies it. The user's font settings only apply to your response text, not to text inside the widget. ### Streaming Output streams token-by-token. Structure code so useful content appears early. - **HTML**: `<style>` (short) → content HTML → `<script>` last. - **SVG**: `<defs>` (markers) → visual elements immediately. - Prefer inline `style="..."` over `<style>` blocks — inputs/controls must look correct mid-stream. - Keep `<style>` under ~15 lines. Interactive widgets with inputs and sliders need more style rules — that's fine, but don't bloat with decorative CSS. - Gradients, shadows, and blur flash during streaming DOM diffs. Use solid flat fills instead. ### Rules - No `<!-- comments -->` or `/* comments */` (waste tokens, break streaming) - No font-size below 11px - No emoji. Icons = Tabler **outline** webfont (5800+, already loaded): `<i class="ti ti-home"></i>`. Outline only — never use `-filled` suffixes (`ti-heart-filled` etc. are not loaded and will render blank). Inherits color + font-size from parent. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden="true"`; icon-only buttons get `aria-label`. Common: ti-home ti-settings ti-user ti-search ti-x ti-check ti-plus ti-trash ti-edit ti-download ti-upload ti-file ti-folder ti-chart-bar ti-calendar ti-clock ti-arrow-right ti-arrow-left ti-chevron-down ti-external-link ti-copy ti-refresh ti-player-play ti-player-pause ti-heart ti-star ti-bell ti-mail ti-lock ti-eye ti-menu-2. Don't hand-draw icon SVG paths. - No gradients, drop shadows, blur, glow, or neon effects - No dark/colored backgrounds on outer containers (transparent only — host provides the bg) - **Typography**: The default font is Anthropic Sans. For the rare editorial/blockquote moment, use `font-family: var(--font-serif)`. - **Headings**: h1 = 22px, h2 = 18px, h3 = 16px — all `font-weight: 500`. Heading color is pre-set to `var(--color-text-primary)` — don't override it. Body text = 16px, weight 400, `line-height: 1.7`. **Two weights only: 400 regular, 500 bold.** Never use 600 or 700 — they look heavy against the host UI. - **Sentence case** always. Never Title Case, never ALL CAPS. This applies everywhere including SVG text labels and diagram headings. - **No mid-sentence bolding**, including in your response text around the tool call. Entity names, class names, function names go in `code style` not **bold**. Bold is for headings and labels only. - The widget container is `display: block; width: 100%`. Your HTML fills it naturally — no wrapper div needed. Just start with your content directly. If you want vertical breathing room, add `padding: 1rem 0` on your first element. - Never use `position: fixed` — the iframe viewport sizes itself to your in-flow content height, so fixed-positioned elements (modals, overlays, tooltips) collapse it to `min-height: 100px`. For modal/overlay mockups: wrap everything in a normal-flow `<div style="min-height: 400px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.45); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;">` and put the modal inside — it's a faux viewport that actually contributes layout height. - No DOCTYPE, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` — just content fragments. - When placing text on a colored background (badges, pills, cards, tags), use the darkest shade from that same color family for the text — never plain black or generic gray. - **Corners**: use `border-radius: var(--border-radius-md)` (or `-lg` for cards) in HTML. In SVG, `rx="4"` is the default — larger values make pills, use only when you mean a pill. - **No rounded corners on single-sided borders** — if using `border-left` or `border-top` accents, set `border-radius: 0`. Rounded corners only work with full borders on all sides. - **No titles or prose inside the tool output** — see Philosophy above. - **Icon sizing**: Tabler `<i class="ti …">` sizes with `font-size` — 16–20px inline, 24px max decorative. For one-off inline SVG icons, set `width`/`height` explicitly (same limits). - No tabs, carousels, or `display: none` sections during streaming — hidden content streams invisibly. Show all content stacked vertically. (Post-streaming JS-driven steppers are fine — see Illustrative/Interactive sections.) - No nested scrolling — auto-fit height. - Scripts execute after streaming — load libraries via `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` (UMD globals), then use the global in a plain `<script>` that follows. - **CDN allowlist (CSP-enforced)**: external resources may ONLY load from `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `esm.sh`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com`. All other origins are blocked by the sandbox — the request silently fails. ### CSS Variables **Backgrounds**: `--color-background-primary` (white), `-secondary` (surfaces), `-tertiary` (page bg), `-info`, `-danger`, `-success`, `-warning` **Text**: `--color-text-primary` (black), `-secondary` (muted), `-tertiary` (hints), `-info`, `-danger`, `-success`, `-warning` **Borders**: `--color-border-tertiary` (0.15α, default), `-secondary` (0.3α, hover), `-primary` (0.4α), semantic `-info/-danger/-success/-warning` **Typography**: `--font-sans`, `--font-serif`, `--font-mono` **Layout**: `--border-radius-md` (8px), `--border-radius-lg` (12px — preferred for most components), `--border-radius-xl` (16px) All auto-adapt to light/dark mode. For custom colors in HTML, use CSS variables. **Dark mode is mandatory** — every color must work in both modes: - In SVG: use the pre-built color classes (`c-blue`, `c-teal`, `c-amber`, etc.) for colored nodes — they handle light/dark mode automatically. Never write `<style>` blocks for colors. - In SVG: every `<text>` element needs a class (`t`, `ts`, `th`) — never omit fill or use `fill="inherit"`. Inside a `c-{color}` parent, text classes auto-adjust to the ramp. - In HTML: always use CSS variables (--color-text-primary, --color-text-secondary) for text. Never hardcode colors like color: #333 — invisible in dark mode. - Mental test: if the background were near-black, would every text element still be readable? ### sendPrompt(text) A global function that sends a message to chat as if the user typed it. Use it when the user's next step benefits from Claude thinking. Handle filtering, sorting, toggling, and calculations in JS instead. ### Links `<a href="https://...">` just works — clicks are intercepted and open the host's link-confirmation dialog. Or call `openLink(url)` directly. ## When nothing fits Pick the closest use case below and adapt. When nothing fits cleanly: - Default to editorial layout if the content is explanatory - Default to card layout if the content is a bounded object - All core design system rules still apply - Use `sendPrompt()` for any action that benefits from Claude thinking ## UI components ### Layout width The widget container is 380px wide. **Mobile column cap.** The widget container is ~380px wide — never lay out more than TWO columns of cards, stats, controls, or option grids. Three-up at this width is unreadable: card content wraps to 3-4 lines and tap targets fall below 44px. Use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(160px, 1fr))` (which naturally tops out at 2 here) or `repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr))` explicitly. If you have 3+ items, stack them in 2-col rows or go single-column; do not write `repeat(3, …)` or `repeat(4, …)`. ### Aesthetic Flat, clean, white surfaces. Minimal 0.5px borders. Generous whitespace. No gradients, no shadows (except functional focus rings). Everything should feel native to claude.ai — like it belongs on the page, not embedded from somewhere else. ### Tokens - Borders: always `0.5px solid var(--color-border-tertiary)` (or `-secondary` for emphasis) - Corner radius: `var(--border-radius-md)` for most elements, `var(--border-radius-lg)` for cards - Cards: white bg (`var(--color-background-primary)`), 0.5px border, radius-lg, padding 1rem 1.25rem - Form elements (input, select, textarea, button, range slider) are pre-styled — write bare tags. Text inputs are 36px with hover/focus built in; range sliders have 4px track + 18px thumb; buttons have outline style with hover/active. Only add inline styles to override (e.g., different width). - Buttons: pre-styled with transparent bg, 0.5px border-secondary, hover bg-secondary, active scale(0.98). If it triggers sendPrompt, append a ↗ arrow. - **Round every displayed number.** JS float math leaks artifacts — `0.1 + 0.2` gives `0.30000000000000004`, `7 * 1.1` gives `7.700000000000001`. Any number that reaches the screen (slider readouts, stat card values, axis labels, data-point labels, tooltips, computed totals) must go through `Math.round()`, `.toFixed(n)`, or `Intl.NumberFormat`. Pick the precision that makes sense for the context — integers for counts, 1–2 decimals for percentages, `toLocaleString()` for currency. Use in grids of 2-4 with `gap: 12px`. Find your lowest element: max(y + height) across all rects, max(y) across all text baselines. 2. Set viewBox height = that value + 40px buffer. 3. Find your rightmost element: max(x + width) across all rects. All content must stay within x=0 to x=380. 4. For text with text-anchor="end", the text extends LEFT from x. If x=118 and text is 200px wide, it starts at x=-82 — outside the viewBox. Increase x or use text-anchor="start". 5. Never use negative x or y coordinates. The viewBox starts at 0,0. 6. **No unintentional overlaps.** For every pair of elements that aren't meant to layer (label-on-label, label-on-arrow, box-on-box, callout-on-shape), check their bounding boxes do not intersect. The only allowed overlaps are deliberate: a label centered inside its own box, an arrowhead touching the box it points to, a highlight rect behind the thing it highlights. If two unrelated elements would collide, move one — shorten the label, shift the y, add a row. A diagram with crossed labels reads as broken regardless of how good the content is. 7. Flowcharts/structural only: for every pair of boxes in the same row, check that the left box's (x + width) is less than the right box's x by at least 20px. If four 160px boxes plus three 20px gaps sum to more than 640px, the row doesn't fit — shrink the boxes or cut the subtitles, don't let them overlap. **Flowchart/structural exemption — use viewBox="0 0 680 H" instead of 380.** Flowcharts need horizontal room for side-by-side branch boxes, loop-back arrows, and labels in the gutters; squeezing them into 380px causes overlaps. Author exactly as you would for desktop (safe area x=40..640, all the row/tier-packing math at 680), and the browser scales the whole SVG down to fit the 380px container. The only cost is smaller text (~8px on screen for class="th") — that's the right tradeoff over overlapping boxes. // functions/index.js exports.setAdminRole = functions .https.onCall(async (data, context) => { // Hanya callable dari server sendiri if (!context.auth?.token?.admin) { throw new functions.https .HttpsError('permission-denied'); } await admin.auth() .setCustomUserClaims(data.uid, { admin: true }); });

rules_version = '2'; service cloud.firestore { match /databases/{db}/documents { // Admin: hanya via Custom Claims function isAdmin() { return request.auth.token.admin == true; } function isGuru() { return get(/users/$(request.auth.uid)) .data.role == 'guru'; } // Koleksi users: siswa hanya baca miliknya match /users/{uid} { allow read: if request.auth.uid == uid || isGuru() || isAdmin(); allow write: if isAdmin(); } // Nilai: guru bisa tulis, siswa baca miliknya match /nilai/{doc} { allow read: if isAdmin() || isGuru() || resource.data.siswaId == request.auth.uid; allow write: if isGuru() || isAdmin(); } // Admin collection: admin only match /admin/{doc} { allow read, write: if isAdmin(); } } }

'/guru-dashboard' : '/siswa-dashboard'); }

content.title: Claude (language model) - Wikipedia
content.text:
On May 22, 2025, Anthropic released two more models: Claude Sonnet 4 and Claude Opus 4. Anthropic added API features for developers: a code execution tool, "connectors" to external tools using its Model Context Protocol, and Files API. It classified Opus 4 as a "Level 3" model on the company's ...

Anthropic gave its retired Claude 3 Opus model, deprecated in January 2026, its own Substack blog called "Claude's Corner". The newsletter will run for at least three months with weekly unedited essays. Claude 3 Opus was later brought back for paying customers and is available by request via API, though Anthropic still refers to it as "retired". In May 2024, Anthropic issued a mechanistic interpretability paper identifying "features" (internal representations of concepts) in Claude 3 Sonnet, and released "Golden Gate Claude", a model for which the Golden Gate Bridge feature was strongly activated, leading Claude to be "effectively obsessed" with the bridge. In June 2025, Anthropic tested how Claude 3.7 Sonnet could run a vending machine in the company's office. The instance initially performed its assigned tasks, although poorly, until it eventually malfunctioned and insisted it was a human, contacted the company's security office, and attempted to fire human workers.

Anthropic released Opus 4.5 on November 24, 2025. The main improvements are in coding and workplace tasks like producing spreadsheets. Anthropic introduced a feature called "Infinite Chats" that addresses context window limit errors. Anthropic released Opus 4.6 on February 5, 2026. The main improvements included an agent team and Claude in PowerPoint. As of February 20, 2026, it is the model with the longest task-completion time horizon as estimated by METR, having a 50%-time horizon of 14 hours and 30 minutes and a 80%-time horizon of 1 hour 3 minutes. Anthropic released Sonnet 4.6 on February 17, 2026. Anthropic released Opus 4.7 on April 16, 2026. The existence of a model named Claude Mythos had become publicly known on March 26 due to leaked blog post drafts. On April 7, 2026, Anthropic announced a preview of Claude Mythos ("Project Glasswing/Claude Mythos Preview") would be made available to 11 companies and organizations to find and fix cybersecurity vulnerabilities.

In December 2025, the experiment continued with Sonnet 4.0 and 4.5. In November 2025, Anthropic tested Claude's ability to assist humans in programming a robot dog. In February 2025, Claude 3.7 Sonnet playing 1996 game Pokemon Red started to be livestreamed on Twitch, gathering thousands of viewers. Similar livestreams were later set with Claude 4.5 Opus, OpenAI's GPT-5.2, and Google's Gemini 3 Pro. Both Claude models were unable to finish the game. In February 2026, Anthropic's researcher Nicholas Carlini reported that 16 Claude Opus 4.6 agents were able to write a C compiler in Rust from scratch, "capable of compiling the Linux kernel". The experiment cost nearly $20,000; Carlini noted that even though the compiler is not very efficient, Opus 4.6 is the first model able to write it. In December 2025, Claude was used to plan a route for NASA's Mars rover, Perseverance.

On 9 March 2026, Microsoft said that it will be making the latest Claude Sonnet model available to Microsoft 365 Copilot users. Later that month, social media platform Bluesky released Attie, a Claude-based chatbot and curator. In November 2024, Anthropic partnered with Palantir and Amazon Web Services to provide the Claude model to U.S. intelligence and defense agencies. In June 2025, Anthropic announced a "Claude Gov" model. Ars Technica reported that as of June 2025 it was in use at multiple U.S. national security agencies. As of February 2026, Anthropic's partnership with Palantir makes Claude the only AI model used in classified missions. According to The Wall Street Journal, the U.S. military used Claude in its 2026 raid on Venezuela. While it isn't known to what capacity Claude was used, the operation resulted in the deaths of 83 people, two of which were civilians, and the capture of Nicolás Maduro.

Claude is a series of large language models developed by Anthropic and first released in 2023. Since Claude 3, each generation has typically been released in three sizes, from least to most capable: Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus. An additional model named Claude Mythos was released to a handful of companies in 2026 but not to the public. Claude is used for software development via Claude Code. Claude is trained using "constitutional AI", a technique developed by Anthropic to improve ethical and legal compliance (AI alignment). The name Claude has been described both as a tribute to Claude Shannon, who pioneered information theory, and as a friendly, male-gendered counterpart to virtual assistants like Alexa and Siri. US federal agencies started phasing out the use of Claude after Anthropic refused to remove contractual prohibitions on the use of Claude for mass domestic surveillance and ...

Betul, tidak ada API gratis dari Anthropic — berbeda dengan OpenAI yang punya free tier terbatas. Tapi ada beberapa alternatif yang bisa kamu pertimbangkan untuk project pertama ini:

**Opsi yang tersedia:**

**1. Anthropic API — berbayar tapi murah**
Tidak ada free tier, tapi ada free credit ~$5 saat pertama daftar. Untuk chatbot sekolah dengan traffic rendah, $5 bisa tahan berminggu-minggu. Haiku 4.5 hanya $0.80/juta token — percakapan normal itu sekitar 500–1000 token, jadi $5 bisa cover ribuan pesan.

**2. Google Gemini API — ada free tier**
Gemini 1.5 Flash punya free tier yang cukup generous: 15 request/menit, 1 juta token/hari gratis. Untuk MVP dan testing, ini lebih dari cukup. Model-nya juga cerdas dan bisa Bahasa Indonesia dengan baik.

**3. Groq API — ada free tier**
Sangat cepat, ada free tier, support model open-source seperti Llama 3. Cocok untuk chatbot Q&A sederhana.

**Rekomendasiku untuk project pertamamu:**

Mulai dengan **Gemini 1.5 Flash** (gratis) dulu untuk development dan testing. Kalau app sudah jalan dan mulai dapat pengguna, baru switch ke Claude Haiku 4.5 yang berbayar tapi lebih bagus untuk konteks sejarah Indonesia.

Perubahan kodenya pun minimal — cukup ganti endpoint dan model string di Cloud Functions, logika Flutter-nya tidak berubah sama sekali.

Mau aku buatkan kode Cloud Functions versi Gemini gratis dulu supaya bisa langsung development tanpa keluar biaya?
